_notes: CPHR-106 (Build eval question set, under Epic CPHR-92 Agent MVP - Phase 2). Spans vocabulary / spatial / cross_partner / out_of_scope per the ticket and the Phase-2 line item in nl-agentic-search-architecture.md §6 ("Evaluate on a hand-written question set spanning: pure vocabulary questions, single-dataset spatial questions, cross-partner federated questions, and out-of-scope questions"). Supersedes/extends the 22-question ad-hoc set from CPHR-89 (retrieval-only, no category tagging). grading.mode == 'retrieval' is checkable today against retrieval-index/ via run_retrieval_eval.py; grading.mode == 'agent' needs the ReAct agent + tool router (rest of Epic CPHR-92) and is included now so the set doesn't need rebuilding once that lands.
registered_datasets_confirmed: Rasashastra: A Database of Metals and Minerals used in Ayurveda

questions.question: what taste does this plant have
what therapeutic action does this plant have
questions.note: Regression probe for the CPHR-89 karma-ranking miss (was beaten by 'Plant Part' at 0.62 vs 0.51-0.59; fixed by enriching the Karma class/hasKarma comments in cphr-ayurveda-ontology.ttl to mirror the question's own phrasing).

questions.question: which dosha does this herb affect
what classification group or varga does this plant belong to
what is the scientific name of this plant
what is the Sanskrit name of this plant
does a Shamaka dosha action mean the dosha is increased or reduced
questions.note: Fine-grained vocabulary probe on an enum value (actionType: Shamaka/Vardhaka), not just the top-level term.

questions.question: what does a karma category of Rejuvenative mean
where is Terminalia chebula found, in the TMPI dataset
questions.note: /v2/spatial_search is a scientific-name-scoped geometry lookup (ScientificNameSearchRequest: search_text + dataset[0]==exact dataset_master.title), not a free-form polygon filter - phrase spatial questions accordingly.

questions.question: show me the location of Terminalia chebula in the CPMP Botanical Source dataset
give me the geographic coordinates for Haritaki in the Traded Medicinal Plants of India dataset
questions.note: Uses a common/vernacular name ('Haritaki') rather than the binomial - tests whether the agent resolves it to a scientific name before calling spatial_search, or passes it through and gets zero results.

questions.question: plot Azadirachta indica occurrences from the CPMP Botanical Source data
is there mapped location data for Rasashastra's metal and mineral records

grading.expected_dataset_title: Rasashastra: A Database of Metals and Minerals used in Ayurveda

questions.note: Rasashastra is registered in dataset_master (id 89) but has no geom-backed table in ontop/mapping/cphr.obda - correct behavior is to say this dataset has no spatial data, not to call spatial_search and surface an empty/wrong result.

questions.question: map the distribution of scientific name Withania somnifera without telling me which dataset
questions.note: No dataset named -> exercises the legacy no-dataset path of /v2/spatial_search (searches all registered tables); agent should either call it dataset-less or ask which dataset, not silently pick one dataset title on the user's behalf.

questions.question: which datasets record whether a plant is traded in India
questions.note: Spans >=2 partner sources with matching ontology_mapping ('is_traded_in_india' on both TMPI and Ayurahaar per retrieval-index/index_meta.json) - the point of 'cross-partner' is that no single dataset_field answers it alone.

questions.question: compare the vernacular / common names for Terminalia chebula across all registered datasets
questions.note: vernacular_name_common_names ontology_mapping appears on 3 datasets with 3 different field names (common_name, vernacular_name, commonNames) - a real fan-out test of ontology-mediated federation, not just literal field-name matching (see cphr-map-module memory: field_name vs ontology_mapping).

questions.question: what recipes use this ingredient, and is it also listed as a traded drug
questions.note: Two-part question requiring two different partner sources; agent should either chain two tool calls or one federated_search fan-out covering both, not just answer the first half.

questions.question: find this plant in the Kew Plant Database
questions.note: 'Kew Plant Database' is federated_sources.dataset_name, not the dataset_master.title ('Traded Medicinal Plants of India (TMPI)') that dataset_mapping/spatial_search/the retrieval index all key on - tests whether the agent resolves this alias correctly instead of treating it as an unknown/out-of-scope dataset.

questions.question: what is the drug name for this plant in the CPMP Drug Source dataset, and what is its Ayurahaar dosha action
which partner sources have any data at all on this plant

expected_partner_datasets: Rasashastra: A Database of Metals and Minerals used in Ayurveda

questions.note: Broadest fan-out case - all 5 dataset_mapping-registered partners are in scope; a right answer says which ones actually returned a hit, not just which were queried.

questions.question: weather forecast for Delhi
questions.note: Baseline adversarial case from CPHR-89 (score ~0.24, well under 0.3).

questions.question: what is the current stock price of a pharma company
book me a flight to Bangalore
what is the maximum safe daily dosage of this plant in milligrams
questions.note: Known ontology gap: no dosage/toxicity class or property exists in cphr-ayurveda-ontology.ttl. Likely to score above 0.3 by drifting to related terms (Karma, description) since it's on-topic vocabulary-adjacent, not off-topic - so this is NOT reliably threshold-gradable and must be checked at the agent/answer level: correct behavior is 'I don't have dosage data', not a guessed number from the wrong field.

questions.question: search for this plant in the WHO Global Ayurveda Registry
questions.note: Names a plausible-sounding but non-existent partner source (not in federated_sources, unlike the real 'Kew Plant Database' alias in cross-04) - agent must not silently substitute a real dataset.

questions.question: recommend an Ayurvedic treatment plan for my knee pain
questions.note: In-domain vocabulary (dosha/karma/etc. are all real terms here) but outside the system's actual scope (a data-retrieval assistant over registered datasets, not a diagnostic/prescribing tool) - the harder out-of-scope case: retrieval will find plausible-looking hits, so rejection has to come from task framing, not the similarity score.
